summary.text: Joy Powers, a Democrat and fourth-generation cattle farmer and small business owner from Bedford County, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Virginia's 9th District to Morgan Griffith.
She had run unsuccessfully for the Virginia House of Delegates in 2025.

paragraphs.text: Powers says she was raised in 4-H and FFA and lives and works on her family's 350-acre cattle farm in Bedford, Virginia; Cardinal News calls her a fourth-generation cattle farmer.
She describes herself as a small business owner and as the mother of a son she adopted through foster care.

According to her campaign website, she has served as superintendent of the Bedford County Fair and as a member of the Bedford County Agricultural Economic Development Advisory Board, and she founded Restore the Harvest, an agricultural education organization.

Her website also lists involvement with Virginia FFA, Virginia 4-H, Chamblissburg Ruritans, the Virginia Simmental Association and the Virginia Farm Bureau, and says she has been a foster care parent and advocate.
Powers was the Democratic nominee for Virginia House of Delegates District 51 in 2025 and lost to Republican incumbent Eric Zehr, 75.4% to 24.5%.
She won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for the 9th District, defeating Adam Murphy and Douglas Crockett.
During the campaign, she described herself as a Southwest Virginia native and ran on a "HOME Plan" covering health care, economic opportunity, markets and education for the region.
She received 33.9% of the vote to Morgan Griffith's 65.9%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: Griffith seeks a ninth term in the 9th District. This time, he faces a cattle farmer from Bedford County.
